minutes.headline: Select Board voted unanimously to let the town manager sign a low-income community solar discount deal.
minutes.summary: The Select Board heard a presentation from the new LEAF education nonprofit and voted unanimously to authorize the town manager to sign onto a Colonial Power Group low-income solar (SMART) discount program. The board also reviewed a draft tri-board communication letter ahead of a budget season expected to be difficult, discussed the finance department's ongoing staffing transition, license renewals, and heard committee reports including the school committee's plan to build three FY27 budget scenarios, before voting to enter executive session on firefighter union bargaining.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to let the town manager sign onto a low-income solar bill discount program with Colonial Power Group, without a town counsel review first.
Board members agreed to individually review a draft joint letter to the finance and school committees ahead of what is expected to be a difficult FY27 budget season, to be discussed next week.

The town is now bargaining with three unions at once; the board voted to enter executive session on firefighter union negotiations, and an initial clerical union bargaining session will be sought for January.
The board voted unanimously to renew all license applications on the agenda, giving applicants with outstanding issues another week to resolve them.
The school committee reported it is building three separate FY27 budget scenarios, per a committee update relayed at this meeting.

why_it_matters: The solar authorization adds a discount on top of the town's existing electricity aggregation rate for UNITIL customers already qualified as low-income -- a bill effect, not a budget one.

The tri-board letter and the school committee's three FY27 scenarios are early signals of how the town, schools and finance office plan to handle a budget season town officials expect to be difficult.
Active bargaining with three unions and an executive session on firefighter contract talks touch town payroll costs that eventually show up in the budget residents vote on.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: Where our minutes and the official minutes overlap — the two votes, most recruitment/finance figures, and most Select Board decisions — they agree closely, with our version mainly missing roll-call detail and misreading several names phonetically. The bigger gap is coverage: our minutes have no record of the LEAF presentation, four deferred New Business items, the Town Manager's Kids Kingdom clarification, most of the committee reports, or the unanimous executive-session vote to bargain with the firefighters' union, all of which the official minutes contain.
